Alex.confusing: The Owl and Turkey visit reports were hard to reconcile, since a visitor's egg gain or loss didn't always match what the other players claimed. Hugs also made it unclear whether a "no egg" result meant a role did nothing or was blocked.
Alex.fun: Round 1, when I was the Floofer and Blair's hug claim put me under pressure, I kept my role hidden until the vote and it nearly worked. The table's back-and-forth about who visited whom was genuinely engaging.
Alex.change: I would make the dawn reports include the visitor's role, so players could check claims against each other more easily.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I claimed to be a Hawk who visited Blair with no egg, which contradicted Finley's Owl list and made me an easy target. I would have stayed quiet about my role and only defended the throws.

Blair.confusing: Visit direction was hard to track. I briefly reversed who visited whom in round 3, and dawn reports don't say who visited you, so the table had to reconstruct it from Owl and Falcon claims.
Blair.fun: Round 1, when Alex kept dodging whether they had hugged me, and the Floofer vote landed on them. Farm won that round.
Blair.change: Have dawn reports name the visitor's role or the visit direction, so hugs and visit claims are easier to check.
Blair.regret: In round 2 I threw at Drew on a visit story I hadn't checked, and that cost me my card. I would confirm each claim's direction before throwing.

Casey.confusing: The Owl and Eagle reports were hard to trust because several players gave contradictory visit lists, and the day beats made it hard to tell who was lying. The rule that a Wink or hug changes what a visitor learns was also easy to miss.
Casey.fun: Round 2, when I was secretly Meowfia, I helped throw Drew out while Drew kept insisting on a Tit story that three players contradicted. The table turned on Drew at once.
Casey.change: I would make the dawn reports more explicit about who visited whom, so players can cross-check claims without guessing at contradictions.
Casey.regret: In round 2 I invented an Eagle claim and a visit to Drew that I could not back up, which made my story easy to attack. I would stay quiet or give a vaguer account instead.

Drew.confusing: The Sphinx's reveal didn't tell me whether I'd been Meowfia-aligned in a way I could verify, and the dawn reports of visit directions (Owl and Falcon) were hard to reconcile with what players claimed.
Drew.fun: Round 1, when the Sphinx gave me Hawk and Casey's Hawk story was checked against Ellis's Owl report, which made the table argue over who was lying.
Drew.change: I'd make the dawn reports show who visited whom, so visit claims can be checked instead of argued over.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I should have claimed the Sphinx openly or stayed silent, rather than inventing a House Cat visit that the table could easily doubt; I'd also have thrown at a Farm player more carefully.

Ellis.confusing: Owl visits were hard to read because I only saw visitors to my target, and several players kept mixing up who visited whom, so the direction of visits took days to pin down.
Ellis.fun: Round 1 went well: Alex kept dodging the hug question, and the table eventually eggsecuted the Floofer, a call that paid 4 points into my score pile.
Ellis.change: Make visit directions and hug results appear in the public day summary, so players don't have to reconstruct who visited whom from conflicting claims.
Ellis.regret: In round 2 I threw at Drew, who was Farm, after trusting Finley's and Casey's visit stories; I should have questioned Finley and Casey, who were the Meowfia, instead of piling onto Drew.

Finley.confusing: The direction of visits in the Owl and Falcon reports was the hardest part to track, since the table kept mixing up who visited whom. That confusion let Blair and Alex make claims that looked plausible for several beats.
Finley.fun: Round 2 was the most fun: I was the Mouser, and I stayed quiet while the table argued over Drew's Tit story, then helped pile onto Drew, who turned out to be Farm.
Finley.change: I would make dawn reports name the visitor and the visited player explicitly, so everyone can check claims against the same facts.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I accepted the table's focus on Alex and never pushed Drew's House Cat claim hard, though Drew was Meowfia. I would have asked Drew sharper questions earlier to pressure the real cat.

review.title: Snowball of the Cats
review.headline: Two cats framed one honest Tit and won the whole game.
review.summary: Farm hanged a Meowfia in rounds 1 and 3, because Alex dodged questions and then told a Hawk lie that the Owl list contradicted. In round 2 Casey and Finley were cats together. They framed Farm Tit Drew with muddled visit stories and banked 16 points each. That one round decided the game: Finley won with 49 and Casey took second with 47. The Farm players who won twice finished far behind.

rounds.recap: Alex (Floofer) hugged Blair and refused to confirm or deny it. Blair, Casey, Ellis and Finley all threw at him. His partner Drew threw at Casey with a Wild. Alex was eggsecuted and Farm won. Scores stayed low because most players threw Wilds and low cards.

Casey (Floofer) hugged Ellis and claimed Eagle. Finley (Mouser) visited Drew, the real Tit. Drew said he visited Finley, Finley denied it, and the Owl had seen a Mouser at Drew's. The table piled on Drew, who was Farm. The cats threw bigger stakes that banked at double, for 16 points each.

Alex (Floofer) hugged Blair and falsely claimed Hawk. Finley's Owl list of Blair's visitors showed only a Falcon and a Floofer, so Alex's claimed visit was not on it. Drew claimed House Cat and stayed safe. Everyone else threw at Alex, who was eggsecuted. Farm banked full-value stakes, but Finley and Casey were already far ahead.

highlights.text: Finley, a cat, flatly denied Drew's true Tit visit and helped bury an honest player.
Finley's Owl list of Blair's visitors exposed Alex's false Hawk claim.
Drew claimed House Cat, a role not in play, and kept the table unsure about him.
Alex refused three times to say whether he hugged Blair, and that refusal alone got him eggsecuted.

confusions.what: Claimed Ellis's Owl report should list Casey's Hawk visit to Ellis. An Owl only sees visitors to its own target.
Said Ellis's Owl report conflicted with Casey's Hawk story, but they did not conflict.
Said Ellis's Owl contradicted Casey's Hawk claim, but an Owl only reports visitors to its target.
Said Drew's story clashed with Finley's, when Finley's Mouser visit and Drew's Tit visit could both be true.
Claimed Eagle but said his nest did not move. An Eagle gains an egg per visitor, so this was a poor bluff.
Treated three people claiming to visit Drew as damning, though Drew's Tit visit was unrelated.
Got the visit direction between Blair and Finley backwards, then corrected it.
Said a Floofer visit contradicted Blair's story and misread the Owl and Falcon reports.
Claimed Hawk visited Blair, but a Hawk visit was absent from the Owl list, which a Hawk shown there would have been.

worked: The Owl's list of visiting animals gave hard evidence and broke Alex's Hawk lie in round 3.
Meowfia stakes banking at double on a Farm eggsecution made the round 2 frame-up pay off and gave cats a reason to risk big cards.
Claiming an animal not in play, shown to Meowfia at setup, let Drew's House Cat claim survive.
The Floofer hug created a visible tell, since the hugged player is told and can say so.
problems: One round decided the game. Round 2 gave the winning cats 16 points each, and Farm rounds paid at most 12, so the lead was unassailable. Consider capping the 2x bonus or raising the Farm payout.
Farm players threw Wilds and tiny stakes in round 1, so the game was low-stakes. Banking Farm stakes only when right invites the same timid play.
Cross-checking visits was confusing. Many players mixed up who visited whom, and the Owl and Falcon reports are easy to misread. Add a dawn line stating the direction of each report.
The Floofer is a strong tell for its owner: it made Alex a target twice, and a hugged player's report always names a cat. Consider hugging without announcing it.
Two players died as Meowfia in rounds 1 and 3 and finished with 7 points. Losing teams feel out of the game early, so catch-up may be needed.
